subject: Evidence & Residency milestone — MAP draft: owners, dates, blockers
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@hearthcare.org>, Emma Smith <emma.smith@medsys.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + proposed milestone owners (evidence, retention)

Thanks Rajiv and Emma — great call today. Per our discussion I captured the primary compliance-related MAP items that matter for HearthCare so we can align owners and a realistic close target. Key outcomes from the call: 

- HearthCare needs: (1) explicit retention windows for PHI-derived artifacts, (2) an event-level audit trail for every inference and admin action, and (3) documented exportability and purge procedures for records tied to patients.
- Hard constraint: PHI must remain within US regions for this pilot; any replication to EU/APAC must be blocked.
- Procurement indicated they will require a BAA and proof of SOC 2 evidence before contract signature.

I'm attaching the SOC2 questions spreadsheet we walked through and a first-pass MAP worksheet (MAP-draft-v2.xlsx) with suggested milestone owners and dates. Proposed milestone snapshot: 

1) MAP Milestone: Data residency & jurisdiction assurance — Owner: Redwood (Rishi) — Target: 2027-05-10 — Dependency: infra region enablement + KMS config
2) MAP Milestone: Retention policy (PHI/PII) — Owner: HearthCare (Rajiv) + Redwood (Marcus) — Target: 2027-05-17 — Dependency: legal sign-off on retention window
3) MAP Milestone: Audit & exportability (event logs + patient export) — Owner: Redwood (Marissa) — Target: 2027-05-12 — Dependency: logging retention config + storage cost estimate

Ask: please confirm owners above and whether the target dates look realistic. Also note any blockers we missed (procurement timelines, internal security reviews, anything else).

Next steps I propose: 
- I will update MAP-draft-v2 with any owner/date changes and share a read-only Drive link.
- Redwood to provide SOC2 artifacts and a short writeup of our audit log retention mechanics (Rishi) by 4/22.

Attachments: SOC2-questions.xlsx (spreadsheet), MAP-draft-v2.xlsx (workbook)

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0124
From: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@hearthcare.org>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Emma Smith <emma.smith@medsys.ai>
Cc: procurement@hearthcare.org
Date: 2027-04-19T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + proposed milestone owners (evidence, retention)

Thanks Marcus. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- Retention: clinical notes derived from model outputs are treated as PHI; we need a default retention ceiling of 7 years for clinical artifacts, but we are open to short-term caches (90 days) for inference performance as long as they are explicitly segregated and auto-purged.
- Audit trails: we require an immutable event-level log for inference calls (timestamp, model id, prompt hash, responder id, dataset tag) and admin actions (exports, key rotations). Those logs must be exportable in a standard CSV/JSON format on request.
- Jurisdiction: pilot must run in us-west-2; any multi-region replication would need a separate procurement path.

Procurement side: I put them on copy. We aim to complete contract review and BAA negotiation by 2027-05-20 if technical items are confirmed this week.

One ask: can you confirm whether Redwood supports per-customer KMS separation (customer-managed keys) for the pilot? That will impact our legal and security assessment.

Rajiv Patel
Head of IT Security
HearthCare
rajiv.patel@hearthcare.org
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@hearthcare.org>, Emma Smith <emma.smith@medsys.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + proposed milestone owners (evidence, retention)

Rajiv — thanks, this is exactly the level of detail we needed. Short answers up front: 

- KMS: yes, we support customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private deployments. For the Hosted API we offer envelope encryption and integration points; we can scope a dedicated key path for the pilot if you prefer (Rishi to confirm technical approach).
- Retention model: Redwood can provide configurable retention buckets: cache (up to 90 days, auto-purge), intermediate (90–365 days), long-term (365–7yrs) with role-based access controls. We'll document the default maps and how to request exceptions.
- Logs: we will produce an event-level audit export (JSON/CSV) and keep a separate immutable write-ahead log for 7 years where required; practical retention for the hosted offering may require additional storage billing.

I've updated MAP-draft-v2.xlsx with Rajiv's retention constraints and pushed a copy to Drive (link below). If owners look good I'll set the target close date to 2027-05-20 to align with your procurement window.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cMAP-draft-v2

Marcus
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@hearthcare.org>
Date: 2027-04-21T08:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + proposed milestone owners (evidence, retention)

Adding a few technical notes for the MAP milestone owners so we have a clear engineering ask: 

- Residency: we can pin the environment to us-west-2 for the pilot. We'll need a small infra ticket to lock down replication and cross-region backups (ETA: 5 business days after go-ahead).
- KMS separation: customer-managed KMS is supported for Dedicated/Private. For Hosted we can implement a dedicated keyspace plus HSM-backed wrapping if procurement requires it — will need legal to accept the SaaS key model vs on-prem HSM.
- Audit & logs: propose the following default config — write-ahead audit log (immutable) retained for 7 years in archival tier, event-level logs (queryable) retained 90 days by default; we can produce on-demand exports of archived logs subject to retrieval cost. If HearthCare needs queryable logs beyond 90 days we should discuss storage/ops cost commitment and SLA.

I'll prepare a short two-page technical note outlining these items and a minimal ticket list for infra and security (will upload to the Drive folder by EOD).

— Rishi
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
From: Emma Smith <emma.smith@medsys.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@hearthcare.org>
Date: 2027-04-22T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + proposed milestone owners (evidence, retention)

Thanks everyone — this is helpful. HearthCare confirms the owners as listed and is comfortable with the proposed process. Two quick notes from ops/procurement: 

- Procurement: aiming for contract sign by 2027-05-20 (aligns to Rajiv's note). They will expect SOC2 Type II evidence and a BAA before signature.
- Ops: will review the 90-day queryable log policy; if we need longer searchable logs we will raise that in the MAP as an optional paid item.

Approved to move forward on the MAP updates — please share the updated MAP-draft-v2 and the technical note from Rishi when ready.

Emma Smith
VP Partnerships & Integrations
MedSys.ai (HearthCare pilot lead)
emma.smith@medsys.ai
